correctness.rationale: Poisson thinning gives independent rate-lambda*theta reset and rate-lambda*(1-theta) flip clocks. A common reset yields uniqueness and exponential coupling. At a stationary exponential reset age, a geometric number of alternating exponential displacement runs has Fourier transform theta*h_plus*(1+(1-theta)*h_minus)/(1-(1-theta)^2*h_plus*h_minus). Direct partial fractions give the two positive decay rates d±, amplitudes A,B, normalization A/d_+ +B/d_- =1, jump A-B=lambda*theta/c, and no atom. Integrating yields negative mass 1/2+[v(1-2theta)-c]/(2D) and mean [c-v(1-theta)]/[lambda*theta*(2-theta)], proving both sharp inequalities and endpoint theta=1. Independent transform and polarity checks corroborate; theta=0 and nonexponential renewal times are not addressed.
